text:
Rachael P (People Ops): Hey team, quick coordination needed — Diego (new hire, O-1) got a consular appointment next Thursday in Madrid and needs an employer support letter + travel/leave confirmation from us. Can we pull this together today?
Jamal K (Eng Manager): Thanks for flagging. I'll draft the role/responsibilities blurb. Travel dates?
Rachael P (People Ops): Appointment is May 3 — Diego will be out May 1–6 (travel day before, buffer after). We need: 1) support letter for consulate, 2) confirmation of employment start & salary for Diego to take to stamping, 3) coverage plan while he's away.
Maria R (Recruiter): I can confirm offer details: start date set to May 17, base salary = EUR 95,000 (converted on offer). I'll upload the signed offer PDF to the candidate folder and share link.
Kevin L (Payroll): Do we need a formal signed SF-50 equivalent? For payroll we just need the signed offer and banking/ID docs by first payroll cutoff. For consulate the salary number + title should be fine.
Legal Bot: Required: an employer support letter on company letterhead stating job title, brief description of duties, salary, start date, and that the candidate is essential. Will also need contact info for consulate follow-up.
Jamal K (Eng Manager): Draft blurb: "Diego will join as Senior Inference Engineer on the Serving Runtime team. He will lead kernel-level latency projects, own production rollouts for model sharding, and mentor 2 ICs. Essential to roadmap items Q3-Q4 (low-latency kernels)." OK?
Rachael P (People Ops): Perfect. Jamal, can you also confirm Diego's manager name & internal project code (for the letter)? We prefer including the hiring manager and a short sentence about why he's critical.
Jamal K (Eng Manager): Manager line: "Reporting to Jamal Khan, Director of Serving Runtime." Project code: SR-KL3 (internal). Add: "Diego's expertise in fused-attention kernels is not easily replaceable within the timeframe of the project."
Rachael P (People Ops): Great. Maria — can you send the candidate's passport name exactly as on passport so the letter matches?
Maria R (Recruiter): Sent via DM to Rachael.
Diego (candidate): Thanks — confirmed passport name, and I can arrive back to Madrid on May 6 if needed. Appreciate the help.
Rachael P (People Ops): Draft support letter below. Please review and sign off so I can put it on letterhead and run by legal: ```[Company Letterhead]
Date: Apr 25, 2026
To: Consulate of Spain (Madrid)
Re: Support for visa stamping — Diego Alvarez

To Whom It May Concern,

Redwood Inference writes in support of Mr. Diego Alvarez's O-1 visa stamping appointment scheduled for May 3, 2026. Mr. Alvarez has accepted an offer to join Redwood Inference as Senior Inference Engineer reporting to Jamal Khan, Director of Serving Runtime. His primary responsibilities will include leading kernel optimization projects for our serving runtime, owning model-sharding rollouts, and mentoring product-focused engineers.

Salary: EUR 95,000 annually.
Projected start date: May 17, 2026.

Mr. Alvarez's specialized skills in attention-kernel fusion are critical to roadmap deliverables in Q3 and Q4, and his absence during the brief travel window will be covered as noted below. Should you require any additional information, please contact Rachael P at people-ops@redwood.ai or +1-415-555-0123.

Sincerely,

Rachael P
People Operations
Redwood Inference
```
Rachael P (People Ops): Coverage plan suggestion: Jamal — can you confirm who will pick up Diego's on-call rotation and initial onboarding tasks May 17–31 if stamping or travel delays occur?
Jamal K (Eng Manager): I'll have Priya cover on-call for the first two weeks. Onboarding tasks: I'll split onboarding checklist between Priya and Luis. They both agreed.
Kevin L (Payroll): Note for benefits enrollment: If Diego's start is delayed beyond May 31 we need the signed offer + I-9 docs before the next benefits cutoff (June 5) to enroll him for June 1 coverage. If stamping takes longer, we can provisionally hold enrollment until docs are complete — but he won't have retroactive coverage.
Rachael P (People Ops): Understood. We'll communicate contingencies in the preboarding note. Maria, please send Diego a short checklist: signed offer, passport scan, preferred bank account details, and availability for a virtual I-9 appointment (we use remote doc review).
Maria R (Recruiter): Will do — sending checklist now and confirming candidate can do the I-9 on April 29.
Diego (candidate): I can do April 29 at 10am PT. Also: will the company provide a travel letter or any reimbursement? My recruiter noted travel stipend on the offer.
Rachael P (People Ops): Yes, travel stipend covered per offer. Maria will share expense process.
Maria R (Recruiter): Expense guide link: https://intranet/redwood/expenses — I'll DM Diego the exact steps and per-diem cap.
Legal Bot: Reminder: once letter is finalized, Legal must review before printing on letterhead. Assign to legal@redwood.ai and allow 24 hours for review.
Rachael P (People Ops): I'll route to Legal after Jamal + Kevin sign off. Can folks ack here when the salary, manager line, and coverage plan are final?
Jamal K (Eng Manager): Ack — manager line and coverage plan final.
Kevin L (Payroll): Ack — salary and payroll notes confirmed.
Maria R (Recruiter): Ack — candidate checklist sent + I-9 scheduled.
Rachael P (People Ops): Thanks — I'll send final letter to Legal and post the signed PDF here once received. :raised_hands:
people-ops-bot: Thread archived to #people-ops for record-keeping.
